english.title: Cause a female 13 or over to engage in a penetrative sexual activity - SOA 2003
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) with intent caused a

(A)_[girl aged 13]_
(B)_[girl aged 14]_
(C)_[girl aged 15]_
(D)_[woman aged 16 or over]_

to engage in sexual activity involving the penetration of

(E)_[her anus]_
(F)_[her vagina]_
(G)_[her mouth with a persons penis]_
(H)_[a person's anus with a part of her body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART OF THE BODY..)]_
(I)_[a person's vagina with a part of her body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART OF THE BODY..)]_
(J)_[a person's anus by her with a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THING..)]_
(K)_[a person's vagina by her with a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THING..)]_
(L)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE ACTIVITIES ARE INVOLVED PLEASE SPECIFY..)]_

when she did not consent and you did not reasonably believe that she was consenting
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4(1) and (4) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Provided the victim was under16 an act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 01/09/1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he/she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom. (section 72).A person guilty of this offence is subject to the notification and orders requirements as provided by Part 2 of this Act which commences at section 80. (Schedule 3 paragraph 17).
(ii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 19).
(iii) Whether a belief is reasonable is to be determined having regard to all the circumstances, including any steps the offender has taken to ascertain whether the victim consented - (section 4(2)).
(iv) See also offence wordings: H5665 - which relates to this offence against by a male person and H5664 - for the non-penetrative offence relating to a female and H5677 for the comparable offence for a girl under13.
(v) IMPORTANT - carefully check an offender's previous convictions. Provisions under sections 224 to 235 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 may mean that s/he is liable to receive a longer sentence if certain conditions apply.
